First, identify a, b, and c. Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If it’s positive, two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex solutions. Plug into the formula and simplify. To find stationary points, first take the derivative f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. It’s like finding still points in a moving landscape—where the slope stops changing.
